questions.stem: Why is cracking carried out on long-chain hydrocarbons?

options.text: To make them safer to transport
To convert excess long-chain fractions into shorter, more useful alkanes and alkenes
To remove sulfur impurities from the fractions
To change them from liquids to gases for storage

questions.explanation: Fractional distillation produces more long-chain hydrocarbons than needed, but there is high demand for shorter molecules like petrol. Cracking breaks long chains into shorter, more useful alkanes (fuels) and alkenes (for making polymers and other chemicals).

questions.stem: What are the conditions for catalytic cracking?

options.text: About 850 degrees C with steam and no catalyst
About 500 degrees C with a zeolite catalyst
Room temperature with a nickel catalyst
About 300 degrees C with a phosphoric acid catalyst

questions.explanation: Catalytic cracking uses a zeolite (aluminosilicate) catalyst at about 500 degrees C and slight pressure. The catalyst lowers the activation energy needed to break C-C bonds. Steam cracking (the other method) uses higher temperatures (~850 degrees C) with steam but no catalyst.
